first.rationale: Competitive entry pricing creates an immediate acquisition risk in price-sensitive SMBs, where inherited evidence indicates targeted promotional pricing can lift acquisition and revenue. A small guarded test is appropriate because the durable, long-term value of discount-acquired accounts—and potential pricing or margin effects—remains uncertain. Onboarding deterioration is also relevant to sustainable revenue, so its prior evidence should be verified before committing.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified source shows higher completion (+13%), faster time-to-value (2.1 days), and improved 30-day retention (+3%), directly addressing the current 4% onboarding-completion decline while supporting sustainable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: its verified acquisition and revenue lift came with 30-day retention down 12%, and the source explicitly rejects it as a sustainable-growth strategy.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment. It is the only verified option that directly improves both a current weakness and downstream durability: completion rose 13%, time-to-value improved by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention rose 3%. The competitor's cut and increased churn urgency do not establish that promotional pricing will retain the existing SMB base; the available pricing evidence instead shows discount-acquired SMB cohorts had 12% lower 30-day retention and is explicitly not sustainable-growth evidence. Churn exposure remains a material risk, but replacing the experiment with deeper discounting would optimize an unverified short-term response at known long-term value risk.
